fields.reasoning: The brief allows pinning a version or deferring; go-runewidth is an indirect dependency whose init runs as soon as a package importing it is linked, so rhiza cannot defer it without restructuring its imports, and a fork or replace would be a new dependency to maintain, which the planner rules forbid.
fields.statement: rhiza's start stops paying go-runewidth's eager init by moving github.com/mattn/go-runewidth (indirect, through charmbracelet/x/ansi) to a released version whose tables build lazily, never by a fork, a replace directive or a vendored copy; if no release does, the builder raises a question instead

fields.acceptance: go build -trimpath -o $TMPDIR/rhiza-x ./cmd/rhiza && GODEBUG=inittrace=1 $TMPDIR/rhiza-x version 2>&1 | grep runewidth shows its init under 2 ms (2026-11-15: 22 ms); go mod why -m github.com/mattn/go-runewidth names the same importers and go.mod has no replace directive; go test -trimpath ./internal/tui/... ./internal/web passes, so text widths are unchanged; failure case: if no released go-runewidth inits lazily, a question blocks this leaf and go.mod is unchanged. Speedup measure: /usr/bin/time -f '%e s' sh -c 'for i in $(seq 200); do $TMPDIR/rhiza-x version >/dev/null; done' against the same loop on 88516d956. Touches go.mod, go.sum.
fields.statement: A rhiza process starts without go-runewidth's eager table init, so a start that never measures text width costs about 17 ms instead of 39 ms, across the 6,600+ rhiza processes cmd/rhiza's scripts start.

fields.acceptance: /usr/bin/time -f '%e s' go test -trimpath -count=1 ./internal/slice -run '^TestFit$' passes within 5 s (2026-11-15: 42 s); go test -trimpath -count=1 -coverprofile $TMPDIR/fit.out ./internal/slice -run '^TestFit$' covers every line of fit's source that the sweep covered on 88516d956; failure case: a state that is skipped or reached out of order (checked by a test case that feeds the checker a hand-made out-of-order sequence) fails with the budget and both states named. Touches internal/slice/budget_test.go only. Must not change fit or loosen what TestFit asserts.
fields.statement: internal/slice's TestFit checks the cut order at the fit's state boundaries instead of fitting at every token budget: it finds the first budget of each cut state by bisection and checks the state just below, at and just above each, plus a fixed seeded sample of budgets between, for both markdown and JSON.
